model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart, labeled Figure 5, compares the per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. The x-axis contains the sparsity rates, ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, while the y-axis represents the perplexity values on a logarithmic scale. The chart features two categories of bars: per-output and per-layer, with the per-output bars generally being shorter than the per-layer bars at lower sparsity rates and significantly taller at higher sparsity rates. The per-output perplexity values range from approximately 5.70 at 10% sparsity to 534.42 at 80% sparsity, while the per-layer perplexity values range from 5.70 at 10% sparsity to 886.10 at 80% sparsity. Notably, both sets of bars increase in height as the sparsity rate increases, with a more dramatic increase observed at higher sparsity rates, particularly between 60% and 80%.
model_annotations.Chinese: 该图比较了不同稀疏率下每输出和每层的困惑度。类别轴是水平的，标记为稀疏率，类别从左到右按升序排列，分别为10%、20%、30%、40%、50%、60%、70%和80%。值轴是垂直的，对数缩放，标记为困惑度，范围从大约5到1000。每输出和每层困惑度的柱状图成对出现，分别用蓝色和橙色表示。每输出的困惑度值从10%稀疏率时的约5.7开始，随稀疏率的增加而增加，80%时达到约1000。每层的困惑度值遵循类似的趋势，从10%时的5.7开始，80%时超过1000。柱状图没有特定的排序，但每对柱状图在视觉上是不同的，蓝色代表每输出，橙色代表每层。
model_annotations.English: This chart illustrates a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. The categories are represented on the horizontal axis, labeled with sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, while the vertical axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale, although the exact label and units are not specified. Two sets of bars are shown, likely representing per-output and per-layer perplexity, with the per-layer perplexity bars being significantly taller at higher sparsity rates. The bars for both categories are relatively short and similar in height at lower sparsity rates, with values around 5.7 to 6.0, but the per-layer perplexity bars increase more sharply at higher sparsity rates, reaching a value of approximately 886.10 at 80% sparsity, while the per-output perplexity bars reach around 534.42. The chart is not explicitly labeled with colors or a legend, but the description under the chart mentions using logarithmic results for comparison due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates. The bars appear to be sorted in ascending order by sparsity rate, and no bars are visually emphasized.
